newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia PM sees 1997 inflation below 8.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia PM sees 1997 inflation below 8.8 pct.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on Tuesday 1997 inflation was expected to be below the 1996 level of 8.8 percent although April monthly inflation jumped to two percent from 0.3 in March.
"We estimate that inflation this year will be at least a bit lower than last year," Drnovsek told a news conference.

He said the government had expected monthly inflation in April to rise due to a 9.5 percent increase in petrol prices at the end of March, adding the government had already raised most prices it planned to this year.
The annual inflation rate rose to 8.2 percent in April from 7.4 percent in March but stood below the 10.7 percent in April 1996. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
